You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 3-chloropyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

picks.reason: Keep the proven L2/B3 pair and test the 5-phenyl regioisomer against the strong A3 additive result.
This tests whether the 4-phenylisoxazole isomer can perform well with the lead catalyst and base.
The dibenzylamino substituent tests whether an electron-rich isoxazole additive improves the lead conditions.
This probes the 3-substituted dibenzylamino isoxazole under the established lead conditions.
The fused benzisoxazole tests whether a rigid bicyclic additive is beneficial with the lead pair.
This evaluates a 5-methyl isoxazole bearing an ester substituent under the best observed catalyst and base.
The alternative ester position tests how isoxazole substitution pattern affects performance with L2/B3.
The dimethylisoxazole tests whether a compact alkyl-substituted additive can approach the A3 result.
The pyrrolyl substituent provides a distinct nitrogen-rich additive to screen with the lead pair.
Testing 5-methylisoxazole with B3 checks whether its earlier weak result was specific to the base.
This ester-substituted regioisomer tests an additional substitution pattern under the lead conditions.
Its prior result with B1 was modest, so testing it with the stronger B3 base checks for a base–additive interaction.
The simple 3-methyl analogue tests whether the favorable A3 motif tolerates replacement of phenyl by methyl.
This isoxazole-4-carboxylate tests an electron-withdrawing substituent at a new ring position.
Although previously weak with a different ligand, this ester additive merits testing with the proven L2/B3 pair.
The methoxy and ester substituents test a more electron-rich, functionalized isoxazole additive.
The difluorophenyl group tests a substituted aryl analogue of the promising phenylisoxazole additive.
This methyl isoxazole carboxylate tests a compact electron-poor additive with the lead catalyst and base.
The furyl-substituted isoxazole tests a heteroaryl additive while retaining the ester functionality.
The thienyl analogue tests whether a sulfur-containing heteroaryl substituent improves the lead conditions.
